question: During which centuries did several Buddhist pilgrims and scholars travel to China on the historic 'silk route'?

options.text: First, second and third centuries AD

solution:
The correct answer is __**First, second and third centuries AD**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Several Buddhist pilgrims and scholars, such as **Faxian**, travelled to China during the first, second, and third centuries AD.
 
• These journeys were primarily taken to collect Buddhist scriptures and spread Buddhism in China.
 
• Notable figures like **Faxian** and **Kashyapa Matanga** played crucial roles in the cultural exchanges between India and China during this period.
 
• The Silk Route was a vital conduit for not only trade but also for cultural and religious exchanges.
 
• These travels significantly influenced the development of Buddhism in China.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Faxian**:

 
 
• Faxian was a Chinese Buddhist monk who travelled to India between 399 and 412 AD to collect Buddhist texts.
 
• His journey is documented in his travelogue, "A Record of Buddhist Kingdoms."
 
 
 
• **Silk Route**:
 
 
• The Silk Route was an ancient network of trade routes that connected the East and West.
 
• It was central to cultural interaction through regions of the Asian continent connecting the East and West from China to the Mediterranean Sea.
 
 
 
• **Buddhism in China**:
 
 
• Buddhism was introduced to China during the Han dynasty (206 BC–220 AD).
 
• It became one of the major religions in China, influencing Chinese culture, philosophy, and art.
 
 
 
• **Kashyapa Matanga**:
 
 
• Kashyapa Matanga was an Indian Buddhist monk who is traditionally thought to have first arrived in China in the 1st century AD.
 
• He is credited with helping to establish Buddhism in China.
